messages:
Nora (Marketing): quick huddle 10am: we need a compact battlecard for next week's partner webinar. top goals: clear benchmark narrative, two SDR hooks, routing rules, and a tiny FAQ.
Ethan (Product Marketing): agree. pitch should emphasize real-world unit economics and long-context reliability rather than raw throughput.
Jin (Field): reps want 10-15 sec soundbites they can use live and in follow-ups. defensible, not hype.
Zoe (Content): i'll draft 3 core claims + 2 bullet datapoints each. let's lock the claims now.
Nora (Marketing): proposed claims: 1) Lower and more predictable unit cost on long-context workloads, 2) One API across hosted/dedicated/private (same SLA and tooling), 3) Built-in fallbacks to maintain availability during capacity events.
Riley (Sales Ops): routing proposal: lead form picks primary interest [Cost / Security / Throughput / Integrations], route by interest + company size. enterprises -> AE queue; proof-of-concept budgets -> SEs; quick trials -> SDRs. add a "benchmark request" checkbox.
Ethan (Product Marketing): benchmark draft: on a 24k token chat sim, Redwood runtime had 1.9x lower GPU token cost vs CloudA baseline when using KV prefix caching; without caching the delta was still 1.4x. will prepare methodology notes.
Zoe (Content): legal check: @Legal Bot — ok to publish comparative ratios if we include methodology and timeframe?
Legal Bot: yes. include exact test dates, model/config, and a link to reproducible results. avoid absolutist language ("always", "never"). comparative language must be fair and reproducible.
Liam (Design): i'll make two quick deliverables: 1-slide benchmark visual and a 1-page SDR leave-behind. need final numbers by tomorrow morning.
Jin (Field): SDR hooks: ops-focused and security-focused. Ops example: "Cut your per-query spend on long chats without sacrificing tail latency15 min to review?" Security example: "Same API, private network + KMS support want our architecture brief?"
Zoe (Content): shortening for email subjects: Ops: "Lower unit cost on long chat"; Security: "Private API + KMS: architecture". Legal Bot: avoid the word "cheaper" in subject lines?
Legal Bot: prefer "lower unit cost" or "more predictable spend". yes, avoid "cheaper".
Ethan (Product Marketing): include a short case snippet: "A payments customer reduced inference spend by ~30% during peak retention windows by enabling prefix caching + tuned batching." mark as 'up to' and cite cohort date.
Riley (Sales Ops): inbound form change: add a required "primary concern" field and a hidden routing signal for estimated ARR (company size tiers). map routing rules in the wiki.
Liam (Design): will use a compact bar viz: tokens per dollar, with tiny footnote for methodology. also provide a small appendix slide with the curl examples for hosted and private endpoints.
Zoe (Content): proposed curl for quick copy/paste: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-7b","input":"...","kv_cache":true,"batch_size":8}'
```
Ethan (Product Marketing): add notes: recommend batch_size 4-8 for interactive long chats, kv_cache on for prefix-heavy flows.
Nora (Marketing): actions: Ethan finalize benchmark doc + raw results link (due EOD tomorrow); Zoe create SDR one-pager + FAQ (due tomorrow AM); Liam design slides + one-pager (due tomorrow AM); Riley update form + routing mapping (due EOD); Jin collect 2 field anecdotes + contact names (due EOD). cc Legal on final copy.
Zoe (Content): putting drafts in drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/marketing/battlecards/field-surge-v1 (placeholder).
Nora (Marketing): avoid comparative absolute claims in socials. use "up to" and include methodology link.
Ethan (Product Marketing): i'll prep a 2-3 sentence webinar narrative readout: "Redwood reduces unit inference spend for long-context workloads through KV prefix caching, workload-aware batching, and optimized kernel selection, delivering predictable economics for production apps."
Liam (Design): will iterate visuals for the "predictable economics" tagline.
Jin (Field): thumbs up. prepping demo snippets to support claims.
Nora (Marketing): if you own an action, react with :white_check_mark:. will sync again tomorrow 9am if needed.
